newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei surges at close, sentiment cautious.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei surges at close, sentiment cautious.

text.p: Strong domestic buying lifted the SIMEX Nikkei futures from their earlier blues to close above the 18,000 level in active trade on Wednesday, dealers said.

A surge on Wall Street on Tuesday, an overnight rebound in their Chicago counterpart and media reports that Japan could lift its tax on securities transaction as early as 1998, were among major factors boosting the Nikkei futures, dealers said.
After rallying to a high of 18,130, the benchmark Nikkei 225 March contract ended at 18,040, up 645 points.
Good buying interest was seen from the big four Japanese banks and a couple of European houses while American brokerage houses were major sellers, dealers said.
Underlying sentiment for the Japanese stock futures remained weak despite Wednesday's rally. Dealers said some houses continued to hold on to their short positions.
On Tuesday, Alan Greenspan's suggestion that there would be no immeidate U.S. rate hikes fuelled the Dow up 40.03 points to end at 6,883.90.
SIMEX March MSCI Taiwan Index ended 2.5 points up at 313.8 on 402 lots. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
